issue.title: Remove Windows Graphics Capture yellow border during screen sharing
issue.body:
## Problem

When FrameRelay shares a display/window using Windows Graphics Capture, Windows draws a colored/yellow border around the captured area.

This border is visually intrusive and should be removed on supported Windows versions.

## Technical direction

Use the official Windows Graphics Capture borderless flow instead of any visual workaround:

- Request `GraphicsCaptureAccessKind.Borderless` through `GraphicsCaptureAccess.RequestAccessAsync(...)`.
- Declare the `graphicsCaptureWithoutBorder` capability in the Windows package manifest where required.
- After access is granted, set `GraphicsCaptureSession.IsBorderRequired = false`.
- Do not emulate removal by cropping frames or covering the border with an overlay.

Microsoft documentation:
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/api/windows.graphics.capture.graphicscapturesession.isborderrequired
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/api/windows.graphics.capture.graphicscaptureaccess.requestaccessasync
- https://learn.microsoft.com/pt-br/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/app-capability-declarations

## Compatibility / fallback

- Detect whether the borderless capture API is available on the running Windows version.
- If the API is unavailable or the user denies borderless access, keep capture working with the normal system border.
- Log the reason for the fallback in diagnostics/log file.
- The application must not fail to start sharing because borderless permission was denied.

## Scope

Apply this to:
- full display sharing;
- single application/window sharing when that capture path is implemented/used.

Do not change:
- WebRTC signaling;
- audio capture;
- encoder/decoder behavior;
- bitrate/FPS logic.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On supported Windows versions, sharing does not show the yellow/colored capture border after the user grants borderless access.
- [ ] Borderless permission is requested using the official Windows API.
- [ ] Required manifest capability is configured for packaged builds.
- [ ] Denied/unsupported borderless capture gracefully falls back to normal bordered capture.
- [ ] Fallback reason is observable in logs/Diagnostics.
- [ ] Existing screen/video/audio streaming continues to work unchanged.
- [ ] Add/update automated tests where feasible around capability detection and fallback behavior.

## Context

Observed during normal FrameRelay screen sharing: the shared monitor gets a yellow outline around the entire captured area.

issue.title: Add Windows MSI installer and publish it with GitHub Releases
issue.body:
## Goal

Add a real Windows MSI installer for FrameRelay so the app is installed as a normal Windows desktop application and appears in **Installed apps / Programs and Features**, with proper uninstall and upgrade behavior.

## Current state

The release workflow already publishes:

- portable `.zip`
- single-file `.exe`
- SHA-256 checksums

`.github/workflows/release.yml` already contains an explicit packaging note saying MSI/setup is intentionally deferred until a `packaging/*.wxs` phase exists, and that **WiX v5 should be pinned** because the current CI is unattended.

The application is Windows-only and currently targets `net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0`.

## Requirements

- Add an MSI packaging project/configuration using **WiX Toolset v5**, following the existing release-workflow decision.
- Package the self-contained Windows x64 application produced by the existing release pipeline.
- Install FrameRelay into a stable Windows install location.
- Register the application in Windows Installed apps / Programs and Features.
- Provide a proper uninstall entry.
- Support clean upgrades between FrameRelay versions without creating duplicate installed-app entries.
- Preserve user data/configuration/logs across upgrades unless a future migration explicitly requires otherwise.
- Use stable product/upgrade identifiers so MSI upgrades continue working across releases.
- Set product metadata consistently:
  - Product name: `FrameRelay`
  - Publisher/author metadata matching the project
  - Version derived from the release version
  - App icon where supported
- Do not introduce FFmpeg/runtime artifacts that were intentionally removed from the project.
- Keep the existing portable ZIP and single-file EXE artifacts; MSI is an additional distribution format, not a replacement.

## Release pipeline

Update `.github/workflows/release.yml` so tagged releases build and upload an MSI asset, for example:

`FrameRelay-win-x64-<version>.msi`

The MSI must also be included in `checksums-sha256.txt`.

The existing release semantics must remain intact:

- pushed `v*` tag -> normal stable release
- manual/PR builds -> prerelease

## Verification

Automate as much verification as practical in CI. At minimum verify that:

- the MSI is produced successfully;
- the MSI contains the expected FrameRelay executable/runtime payload;
- the release workflow uploads the MSI;
- the checksum file includes the MSI;
- install -> app launches;
- upgrade -> existing installation is upgraded rather than duplicated;
- uninstall -> application files are removed while user-owned data/logs remain intact.

## Out of scope

- Auto-update behavior itself. That belongs to a separate updater issue.
- Linux/macOS packaging.
